p: first month: This is a notable example for all princes, first to establish the pure religion of God and to procure that the Lord may be honoured and served correctly.
doors of the house of the: Which Ahaz had shut up, 2Ch 28:24.
the filthiness out of the holy: Meaning, all the idols, altar groves and whatever was occupied in their service and with which the temple was polluted.
Wherefore the wrath of the LORD: He shows that the contempt of religion is the cause of all God's plagues.
turn away from us: He proves by the judgments of God on those who have contemned his word, that there is no way to avoid his plagues, but by conforming themselves to his will.
cleanse it: From the pollution and filth that Ahaz had brought in.
first month to sanctify: Which contained part of March and part of April.
rose early: By this manner of speech the Hebrews mean a certain diligence and speed to do a thing: and when there is no delay.
sprinkled it on the altar: For without sprinkling of blood nothing could be sanctified, He 9:21, Ex 24:8.

and they laid their hands upon: That is, the king and the elders, as in Le 4:15 for they who offered a sin offering must lay their hands on it, to signify that they had deserved that death, and also that they consecrated it to God to be sanctified by it, Ex 29:10.
commandment of the LORD by his: This thing was not appointed by man, but it was the commandment of God.
LORD began also with the trumpets: The psalm which David had appointed to be sung for thanksgiving.
by David king of Israel: Which David had appointed to praise the Lord with.
words of David: With the psalm mentioned in 1Ch 16:8.
consecrated things were six hundred oxen: That is, for the holy offerings.
more upright in heart to sanctify: Meaning, were more zealous to set forth the religion.
prepared the people: He shows that religion cannot proceed unless God touches the heart of the people.
